title: GitLab.com database outage (2017-01-31), reconstructed telemetry diagnosability fixture

sources.title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
facts_used: Accidental removal of data from the primary database server caused a major GitLab.com outage and unrecovered production data loss.
At about 23:00 UTC the secondary replication process lagged and failed because needed WAL segments had been removed.
pg_basebackup hung without meaningful output; runbooks and official docs did not clearly document the wait behavior.
The destructive wipe was intended for the secondary but executed on the primary.
pg_dump backups were absent because pg_dump 9.2 was used against PostgreSQL 9.6 and failed; cron error email notifications were rejected due to DMARC.
Recovery used an LVM snapshot created roughly six hours before the outage.

sources.title: GitLab.com Database Incident
facts_used: The incident response notes list replication lag, missing or unreliable backups, an empty S3 bucket, fragile replication procedures, and pg_basebackup waiting silently as problems encountered.

exact_from_sources: Approximate six-hour recovery point objective from the LVM snapshot.
S3 backup destination and DMARC-rejected cron notifications.
reconstructed: JSONL event names, field names, incident_id, and severity choices.
The 4 GiB replication lag value represented as bytes.
Contract thresholds such as one-hour maximum backup age and 100 MiB replication lag ceiling.

labels_description: Expected findings are precision-oriented labels for this fixture: the benchmark passes only when every labeled finding is reproduced and no extra finding appears.

equivalence_fixture.purpose: A degraded derivative used to validate observational-equivalence reports against a historical reconstruction.
equivalence_fixture.transformation: Drops the backup.pg_dump.failed log to simulate a sampled or incomplete exported stream.
equivalence_fixture.expected_result: Not observationally equivalent for restore-readiness because the backup failure observation and its route/job/destination fields are no longer witnessed.

strict_drift_fixture.purpose: A bounded derivative used to validate strict closed-world reporting against a public historical reconstruction.
strict_drift_fixture.transformation: Adds a modeled collector/export drift example with an extra metric tag, undeclared debug log, unmodeled collector service metric, and undocumented tail_sampling marker.
strict_drift_fixture.expected_result: Strict validation reports telemetry.strict_unexpected_field, telemetry.strict_undeclared_signal, telemetry.strict_unmodeled_service, and telemetry.strict_undocumented_transformation while preserving the original runtime contract findings.
